patch.author: Christopher Owen <christopherowen@users.noreply.github.com>, Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:37:19 +0000 (kept)
patch.subject: perf(worker): trim the host heap once when startup freezes the GC heap
applies: git am on candidate-53's tree before 0784 (0781 included); 0785 still applies on top
git am on candidate-53 without #960, #998 and #984 (the overlay's base); result equals overlay/
files: vllm/utils/gc_utils.py (+2: trim_host_heap() in freeze_gc_heap before gc.freeze)

verdict_detail: #984 round 1 is the end-of-startup host-heap trim and nothing else. It removes all of round 0's startup cost and its decode-path flush, and keeps round 0's whole host-memory reclaim at readiness. The reclaim is small: the worker's RssAnon is 64-84 MiB lower at ready, and round 0's TP3 floor gain was 0.03-0.12 GiB a rank. The decisive TP3 boot will most likely show the floor 'same', not higher beyond the interval. If it does, #984 has no serving metric left and should be dropped: no-defensible-correction at that point.

where_the_77s_went.answer: Round 0 added gc.collect() (plus trim_host_heap()) to release_device_memory_under_pressure(), 1107's UMA flush. process_weights_after_loading() calls that function after every quantized module. Under UMA pressure on a TP3 rank it releases 277 times across the target's and the draft's post-processing, and each full gc.collect() of the loaded heap takes about 0.25 s. The trims are not the cost: 302 trim_host_heap() calls took 0.08 s in all.

tp3_switched_sp5_engine_logs.source: read only: candidate-53-no960-no998-again (with #984) and candidate-50-no1009 (without) engine logs, the same images as the attribution arms (the attribution boots saved no engine logs)

sp8_one_rank_startup_phases_s.how: raw/sp8/harness/boot_tp3r0.py: the real engine startup of tp3-switched rank 0 (1107 recipe arguments and environment, rank-0 shard: 92.88 GiB weights, 4.91 GiB KV; the memory breakdown matches sp5 rank 0's) on one GB10, with a 3-rank fake process group. Same session, two boots of each arm, order base, fix, c984, c984, fix, base, after one warm-up boot (warm-fix).

memory.reading: fix and c984 end startup with the same anonymous RSS (2746 MiB mean each, against base's 2820 MiB). So round 0's 300 mid-startup trims add nothing to the state at readiness, which is where the floor is set (sp5 and sp8 both record the minimum at ready). The 66 MiB from the kept trim is below MemAvailable's boot-to-boot spread on sp8 (about 0.15 GiB), so the floor rows show 'same' there. On TP3, round 0 gave the floor 0.03-0.12 GiB a rank, matching about 70 MiB. In serving the engine-core and API-server processes also run the trim in their freeze_gc_heap (7 MiB more here, in process). CUDA allocator slack is 575 MiB in every arm: the added gc.collect() calls before empty_cache freed nothing.
memory.kv_capacity: unchanged; the recipe fixes --kv-cache-memory-bytes (5,485,052 tokens in every arm)

kept: trim_host_heap(): mimalloc mi_collect(true) in libc10 (symtab resolution) + glibc malloc_trim(0)
one call in freeze_gc_heap() after its last collection: the worker, engine core and API server each reach it at the end of startup; 66 MiB, 5 ms, on rank 0's worker
tests: test_freeze_gc_heap_trims_before_freeze, test_trim_host_heap_reclaims_cpu_tensor_and_glibc_arenas (+ import pytest, which it calls)

dropped.what: the post-prefill flush (_pending_post_prefill_cache_flush, _last_batch_cg_mode, reclaim_uma_memory() on the first FULL decode step after an eager step, in execute_model and sample_tokens)
dropped.why: blocks the host 32-35 ms (116-120 ms unfrozen) on the decode path. The next prefill takes about 61-67 ms to remap the memory (own-mark flush984). With --prefill-yield short, decode steps run between a long prefill's chunks, so it runs after every chunk.

attribution_note.finding: In the round-0 attribution table, with #984 against without it, stall-3 prefill 131,072 under decode is -2.37% (margin 1.27%), and decode step p90 during the prefill is +0.77% (interval 0.30%), both verdict 'worse'. The repeat of the arm without #984 is 'same' (+0.55%). attribute-stall3 shows candidate-53 without #984 'same' as candidate-50 (+0.49%). The brief and the merged receipts README (6cac4642) say stall-3 is unchanged and call the screen's 2.1% stall-3 gap drift. The table instead puts that gap on #984, consistent with the post-prefill flush running after every chunk. Round 1 removes the flush.

decisive_check.what: tp3-switched boot (coordinator): candidate-53 image + overlay/ (16 files, the same set as no960-no998-no984/overlay). Suggested profile: tp3-switched-no960-no998-984r1.json, whose mounts assume the overlay is committed at candidate-53/984r1/overlay. ABBA against tp3-switched-no960-no998-no984.json, with startup memory and prefill-stall3-suite.json.

expect.startup_floor: about +0.07 GiB a rank, likely within the interval

fidelity_limits_sp8: One rank: collectives move no data (fake group, PyNCCL stand-in, no sparknet one-shot), so forward values are not meaningful and graph capture holds no NCCL or sparknet buffers. Capture's logged memory is a free-memory delta and is noisy on one node: -0.63 to +0.84 GiB across the six boots, against 1.65-1.75 GiB at TP3. B12X preparation decides on rank 0 alone, and the startup rendezvous returns at once.
EngineCore runs in the worker's process (external launcher), so the engine core's freeze_gc_heap trim lands in the same RSS; the API server is not started.
Model loading on sp8 is 40 s against 40.7 s on sp5; preparation 23.5 s against 23.7 s; round 0's load is 109 s against 110 s: the phases match TP3 rank 0.
